decision_cruda.rationale: LH-03 is down at N574-02 but the repair is in place and expected by 09:45-10:00 (likely 09:54). The radio and CMMS agree. Norte is already truck-limited: inflow is 71 t/h against 66 t/h truck capacity, and its stockpile is 242 of 450 t. A loan would lose its travel time, take production or development from the lender, and add almost nothing. Only a stope in loading phase or a heading can lend a loader, and moving one would cost more than the ~0.5 h outage. Making no move is best.

LH-03 is down until about 15:30 or later (CMMS and radio agree). Norte is already truck-limited (inflow 71 vs 66 t/h) with 245 t in the stockpile, and Central is also truck-limited (96 vs 91). A loan to N574-02 would add nothing. Este has truck spare capacity (inflow 33 vs 72 t/h). LH-05 alone loads about 214 t of the 269 t at E543-11 by 17:00. A second loader recovers about 55 t at 8.3 g/t, which is roughly 14.7 oz. LH-10 leaves the workshop at 11:00, arrives at 11:30 and has no home place to lose. LH-08 would cost 0.2 oz/h and LH-09 costs 4 oz/h, so I leave both where they are.
